		-- Defer the listener body. RBXScriptSignal connection order isn't guaranteed,
		-- so without defer this listener can fire before the plugin's main selection
		-- listener has refreshed ctx.currentTransformed  -  leaving the panel one step
		-- behind the user's actual selection (e.g. select 2 → no change, select 3 →
		-- shows "2 selected"). Defer to the next resumption so handleSelection has
		-- finished updating ctx before we read it.
		if _selectionConn then _selectionConn:Disconnect() end
		_selectionConn = Selection.SelectionChanged:Connect(function()
			task.defer(function()
				if not _open then return end
				local nextItems = _collectFromSelection()
				if _sameItems(_items or {}, nextItems) then return end
				_reinitFromSelection(nextItems)
				M.populateSections()
			end)
		end)
	end

	function M.rollAll() _rollBatch() end

	function M.apply()
		if not _open then return end
		-- Skip waypoints when both batches are empty. Walks nested itemBatch tables
		-- since `next()` on the outer table alone passes for `{[item]={}}`.
		if not _batchHasEntries(_lastBatch) and not _batchHasEntries(_retainedBatch) then
			M._teardown()
			return
		end
		CHS:SetWaypoint("Part-Icles: Before Randomize")
		-- Restore baseline + replay both retained AND last batches atomically so undo
		-- captures one diff and so retained pinned values commit alongside fresh rolls.
		_restoreSnapshots()
		_replayBatch()
		CHS:SetWaypoint("Part-Icles: Randomize")
		M._teardown()
	end

	function M.cancel()
		if not _open then return end
		-- Scoped restore (Modules/Randomizer/Cancel.luau): only revert props the
		-- Randomizer wrote during this open session, so unrelated edits survive.
		Cancel.restoreTouchedOnly({
			snapshots = _snapshots,
			lastBatch = _lastBatch,
			retainedBatch = _retainedBatch,
			QOL = QOL,
		})
		M._teardown()
	end

	-- Palette dropdown's expanded options frame parents to ScreenGui (escapes ScrollingFrame
	-- clipping); hiding the panel doesn't destroy it. AND makeDropdown toggles the ancestor
	-- ScrollingFrame's `ScrollingEnabled` on MouseEnter/Leave so MouseWheel only cycles
	-- dropdown options instead of scrolling the section list  -  if populate or teardown fires
	-- while the cursor is on the dropdown, MouseLeave never runs and the scroll stays stuck.
	-- Helper pairs the dismiss with the defensive restore so both call sites (populateSections
	-- and _teardown) stay in sync.
	local function _closeDropdownUi()
		if Widgets.hideDropdownExpansion then Widgets.hideDropdownExpansion() end
		if panel.sectionList then panel.sectionList.ScrollingEnabled = true end
	end

	function M._teardown()
		_snapshots = nil
		_items = nil
		_itemTypeName = {}
		_lastBatch = nil
		_retainedBatch = nil
		_checked = {}
		_open = false
		for _, conn in ipairs(_toggleConns) do conn:Disconnect() end
		_toggleConns = {}
		_resolvedLinks = {}  -- clear sanitized-link cache so next open re-reads attrs
		-- Drop the SelectionChanged hook so closed panels stop reacting.
		if _selectionConn then _selectionConn:Disconnect(); _selectionConn = nil end
		_closeDropdownUi()
		panel.panel.Visible = false
	end

	-- Read accessor for UI populate. Takes (typeName, propKey)  -  composite key.
	function M.isChecked(typeName, propKey) return _checked[_compKey(typeName, propKey)] == true end
	-- Read accessor so toolbar can branch open/cancel.
	function M.isOpen() return _open end

	-- Recompute a section header's tristate glyph from current _checked. Called whenever any
	-- contained-row toggle flips OR when the user clicks the header itself.
	local function _refreshHeaderGlyph(sectionName, glyphLabel)
		local props = _sectionProps[sectionName]
		if not props or #props == 0 then glyphLabel.Text = "[ ]"; return end
		local on = 0
		for _, k in ipairs(props) do if _checked[k] then on = on + 1 end end
		if on == 0 then glyphLabel.Text = "[ ]"
		elseif on == #props then glyphLabel.Text = "[X]"
		else glyphLabel.Text = "[~]" end
	end

	-- Build sectionList. Listens for IsOn AttributeChanged on each Widgets.makeToggle so
	-- _checked stays in sync without stacking another Activated handler.
	-- UI polish:
	--   - Tristate section headers via a TextButton glyph ([ ] / [~] / [X]). Click cycles
	--     all-or-none (off if any-on, else on for every prop in the section).
	--   - Mixed link-state qualifier appended to axis-prop row labels when items in the
	--     frozen selection disagree on link state.
	function M.populateSections()
		-- Rebuilding rows must dismiss any open palette dropdown AND restore the section
		-- ScrollingFrame's `ScrollingEnabled` (in case populate fires while cursor is on
		-- the dropdown  -  same edge case as _teardown). _closeDropdownUi pairs both.
		_closeDropdownUi()
		for _, child in ipairs(panel.sectionList:GetChildren()) do
			if child:IsA("TextLabel") or child:IsA("Frame") then child:Destroy() end
		end
		for _, conn in ipairs(_toggleConns) do conn:Disconnect() end
		_toggleConns = {}
		_sectionProps = {}
		_sectionHeaderRefresh = {}
		_typeRowToggles = {}
		_typeHeaderRefresh = {}
		-- Tree-style sections  -  top-level type header ("TypeName (N selected)") with
		-- category sub-headers (Spawning / Appearance / ...) underneath. Mirrors
		-- Properties panel hierarchy. typesInSel gates `randomizableSectionsByType` so
		-- other types' props don't render. countByType drives the per-type-header count.
		local typesInSel = {}
		local countByType = {}
		if _items then
			for _, e in ipairs(_items) do
				typesInSel[e.typeName] = true
				countByType[e.typeName] = (countByType[e.typeName] or 0) + 1
			end
		end
		local sections = PropertyCatalog.randomizableSectionsByType(TypeRegistry, PE_SECTIONS, Rules, typesInSel)
		local Th = Theme
		local W = Widgets

		-- Top-row "Group axes" toggle. Defaults ON; M.open() re-arms `_groupAxes = true`
		-- each session. Tooltip-style label clarifies that this couples X/Y/Z to a
		-- single magnitude family rolled once per (typeName, family). Blob-wrapped to
		-- match Settings AERow / Shortcut row convention.
		local groupRow = W.makeBlob("GroupAxesRow", panel.sectionList, UDim2.new(1, -8, 0, 22))
		groupRow.LayoutOrder = -1  -- ensure ordering above sections
		W.addPadding(groupRow, 8, 4, 0, 0)
		local groupLbl = W.makeLabel("L", groupRow, "Group axes (X/Y/Z share one rolled value)",
			Th.MutedGold, Th.Font, 9)
		groupLbl.Size = UDim2.new(1, -28, 1, 0)
		local groupToggle = W.makeToggle("GroupAxes", groupRow)
		groupToggle.Position = UDim2.new(1, -26, 0.5, -8)
		groupToggle:SetAttribute("IsOn", _groupAxes)
		local groupConn = groupToggle:GetAttributeChangedSignal("IsOn"):Connect(function()
			_groupAxes = groupToggle:GetAttribute("IsOn") == true
			-- Drop the retained batch on flip  -  its entries were keyed by origins
			-- under the OLD grouping convention (family.primary when grouped, raw
			-- propKey otherwise). Keeping them through a flip means the re-check
			-- pruning matches against new origins and silently leaks old writes
			-- through Apply. Reset to baseline + re-roll so the user sees the
			-- grouped/ungrouped variant from a clean slate.
			_retainedBatch = nil
			_restoreSnapshots()
			if _lastBatch then _rollBatch() end
		end)
		table.insert(_toggleConns, groupConn)

		-- Top-row "Randomize Keypoint Count" toggle. OFF (default):
		-- NumberSequence emits 2 keypoints (start + end with random envelopes);
		-- ColorSequence emits 2 palette-honoring keypoints. ON: NumberSequence emits 3..7
		-- keypoints; ColorSequence emits 3..6 palette-honoring keypoints. Either way the
		-- palette dropdown stays meaningful  -  it controls hue family in both shapes.
		local kpRow = W.makeBlob("RandomizeKeypointsRow", panel.sectionList, UDim2.new(1, -8, 0, 22))
		kpRow.LayoutOrder = -1
		W.addPadding(kpRow, 8, 4, 0, 0)
		local kpLbl = W.makeLabel("L", kpRow, "Randomize Keypoint/ColorSequence Count",
			Th.MutedGold, Th.Font, 9)
		kpLbl.Size = UDim2.new(1, -28, 1, 0)
		local kpToggle = W.makeToggle("RandomizeKeypoints", kpRow)
		kpToggle.Position = UDim2.new(1, -26, 0.5, -8)
		kpToggle:SetAttribute("IsOn", _randomizeKeypoints)
		local kpConn = kpToggle:GetAttributeChangedSignal("IsOn"):Connect(function()
			_randomizeKeypoints = kpToggle:GetAttribute("IsOn") == true
			if _lastBatch then _rollBatch() end
		end)
		table.insert(_toggleConns, kpConn)

		-- Top-row "Reset to initial on uncheck" toggle. ON (default): unchecking
		-- a prop reverts the live preview to its snapshot value. OFF: unchecking just drops
		-- the prop from the apply-batch  -  already-rolled visual stays so the user can roll
		-- one prop, untick it (keeps showing), and roll another while still seeing both.
		-- Apply still skips unchecked props in either mode.
		local resetRow = W.makeBlob("ResetOnUncheckRow", panel.sectionList, UDim2.new(1, -8, 0, 22))
		resetRow.LayoutOrder = -1
		W.addPadding(resetRow, 8, 4, 0, 0)
		local resetLbl = W.makeLabel("L", resetRow, "Reset to initial on uncheck",
			Th.MutedGold, Th.Font, 9)
		resetLbl.Size = UDim2.new(1, -28, 1, 0)
		local resetToggle = W.makeToggle("ResetOnUncheck", resetRow)
		resetToggle.Position = UDim2.new(1, -26, 0.5, -8)
		resetToggle:SetAttribute("IsOn", _resetOnUncheck)
		local resetConn = resetToggle:GetAttributeChangedSignal("IsOn"):Connect(function()
			_resetOnUncheck = resetToggle:GetAttribute("IsOn") == true
			-- Flipping ON means "drop pending values on uncheck"  -  but uncheck-then-
			-- flip leaves a retained batch from the OFF era that Apply would still
			-- commit. Clear it + restore baseline so the toggle's user-promise holds.
			if _resetOnUncheck and _retainedBatch then
				_retainedBatch = nil
				_restoreSnapshots()
				_replayBatch()
			end
		end)
		table.insert(_toggleConns, resetConn)

		-- Bucket sections by typeName so we can emit a top-level type header once per
		-- type, then list that type's category sub-sections beneath it.
		local sectionsByType = {}
		local typeOrder = {}
		for _, sec in ipairs(sections) do
			if not sectionsByType[sec.typeName] then
				sectionsByType[sec.typeName] = {}
				table.insert(typeOrder, sec.typeName)
			end
			table.insert(sectionsByType[sec.typeName], sec)
		end
		for _, typeName in ipairs(typeOrder) do
			-- Type group is wrapped in a TypeContainer Frame so the type-level collapse
			-- arrow can hide everything beneath the type header in one flip. Container
			-- holds {typeHdr, typeChildren}. typeChildren holds all category section
			-- blobs + their sectionBody Frames. Collapse arrow on typeHdr toggles
			-- typeChildren visibility.
			local typeContainer = Instance.new("Frame")
			typeContainer.Name = "TypeContainer_"..typeName
			typeContainer.BackgroundTransparency = 1
			typeContainer.AutomaticSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.Y
			typeContainer.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 0)
			typeContainer.Parent = panel.sectionList
			W.addListLayout(typeContainer, 4, Enum.FillDirection.Vertical)

			local typeHdr = W.makeBlob("Type_"..typeName, typeContainer, UDim2.new(1, -8, 0, 26))
			W.addPadding(typeHdr, 4, 4, 0, 0)
			-- Type-level tristate glyph (parent of all categories' rows for this type).
			local typeGlyph = Instance.new("TextButton")
			typeGlyph.Name = "TypeGlyph"
			typeGlyph.BackgroundTransparency = 1
			typeGlyph.Text = "[ ]"
			typeGlyph.Font = Th.Font; typeGlyph.TextSize = 12; typeGlyph.TextColor3 = Th.BrightGold
			typeGlyph.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left
			-- Tighter glyph spacing  -  bracket text only takes ~14px so a 28px box left
			-- huge gaps between [ ] and the label. Drop to 16px.
			typeGlyph.Position = UDim2.new(0, 16, 0, 0); typeGlyph.Size = UDim2.new(0, 16, 1, 0)
			typeGlyph.Parent = typeHdr
			-- Friendly display name from TypeRegistry uiSection. PE has no TypeRegistry
			-- entry (raw ParticleEmitter); BuildProperties banners it as "Particles"  - 
			-- mirror that here.
			local typeDef0 = TypeRegistry.Types[typeName]
			local displayName = (typeDef0 and typeDef0.uiSection)
				or (typeName == "PE" and "Particles")
				or typeName
			local typeLbl = W.makeLabel("L", typeHdr,
				("%s (%d selected)"):format(displayName, countByType[typeName] or 0),
				Th.BrightGold, Th.Font, 12)
			typeLbl.Position = UDim2.new(0, 34, 0, 0)
			typeLbl.Size = UDim2.new(1, -38, 1, 0)
			typeLbl.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left

			local typeChildren = Instance.new("Frame")
			typeChildren.Name = "TypeChildren_"..typeName
			typeChildren.BackgroundTransparency = 1
			typeChildren.AutomaticSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.Y
			typeChildren.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 0)
			typeChildren.Parent = typeContainer
			W.addListLayout(typeChildren, 4, Enum.FillDirection.Vertical)
			-- Left-indent so categories visually nest under their type header.
			W.addPadding(typeChildren, 12, 0, 0, 0)
			W.addCollapseButton(typeHdr, {typeChildren}, {anchorLeft = true, arrowPos = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0)})

			_typeRowToggles[typeName] = {}
			local typeNameRef = typeName
			local typeGlyphRef = typeGlyph
			_typeHeaderRefresh[typeName] = function()
				local lst = _typeRowToggles[typeNameRef]
				if not lst or #lst == 0 then typeGlyphRef.Text = "[ ]"; return end
				local on = 0
				for _, e in ipairs(lst) do if _checked[e.comp] then on = on + 1 end end
				typeGlyphRef.Text = (on == 0 and "[ ]") or (on == #lst and "[X]") or "[~]"
			end
			local typeGlyphConn = typeGlyph.Activated:Connect(function()
				local lst = _typeRowToggles[typeNameRef]
				if not lst then return end
				local anyOn = false
				for _, e in ipairs(lst) do if _checked[e.comp] then anyOn = true; break end end
				local target = not anyOn
				for _, e in ipairs(lst) do e.toggle:SetAttribute("IsOn", target) end
			end)
			table.insert(_toggleConns, typeGlyphConn)

			-- Per-section emission extracted to RandomizerSection sibling. Pass the bag
			-- of shared mutable refs + helpers; mutable scalars come through getters so
			-- the section's row closures see live values.
			local sectionBag = {
				W = W, Th = Th, TypeRegistry = TypeRegistry, Rules = Rules,
				checked = _checked, paletteMode = _paletteMode, itemTypeName = _itemTypeName,
				sectionProps = _sectionProps, sectionHeaderRefresh = _sectionHeaderRefresh,
				typeRowToggles = _typeRowToggles, typeHeaderRefresh = _typeHeaderRefresh,
				toggleConns = _toggleConns, AXIS_TO_FAMILY = AXIS_TO_FAMILY, compKey = _compKey,
				hasMixedLinkState = _hasMixedLinkState, refreshHeaderGlyph = _refreshHeaderGlyph,
				restoreSnapshots = _restoreSnapshots, replayBatch = _replayBatch, rollBatch = _rollBatch,
				getLastBatch = function() return _lastBatch end,
				getGroupAxes = function() return _groupAxes end,
				getResetOnUncheck = function() return _resetOnUncheck end,
				getOrInitRetainedBatch = function()
					_retainedBatch = _retainedBatch or {}
					return _retainedBatch
				end,
			}
			for _, sec in ipairs(sectionsByType[typeName]) do
				local sectionUid = _compKey(sec.typeName, sec.name)
				RandomizerSection.emit(sectionBag, sec, sec.typeName, sectionUid, sec.name, typeChildren)
			end
		end
		-- Empty-selection hint blob: distinguishes "empty" from "loading" when no
		-- type sections render. Non-interactive; follows the row blob convention.
		if #typeOrder == 0 then
			local emptyBlob = W.makeBlob("EmptyHint", panel.sectionList, UDim2.new(1, -8, 0, 22))
			W.addPadding(emptyBlob, 8, 4, 0, 0)
			local emptyLbl = W.makeLabel("L", emptyBlob,
				"No transformed items selected", Th.DarkGold, Th.Font, 10)
			emptyLbl.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left
		end
	end

	return M
end

children.name: RandomizerWriter
children.source:
--[[
	RandomizerWriter  -  Part-Icles V5
	Copyright (C) 2026 Qwinkle

	Per-prop write dispatch for the Randomizer:

	- Virtual emit attrs (`virtualEmitAttr = true` in rule) -> `item:SetAttribute(propKey, value)`
	  because EmitCount/EmitDelay/EmitDuration live on the item, NOT in PartIcleProperties.
	- Everything else -> `TypeRegistry.write(item, propKey, value)` so attrName / nonNegative
	  / directAccess Trail dispatch all happen via the existing TypeRegistry pipeline.
	- For graph (NumberSequence / ColorSequence) writes, ALSO clear the `<propKey>_BezierHandles`
	  attribute on the Configuration. Old handles don't match new keypoints; leaving them in
	  place would make the Graph editor open with junk on next select.
]]

local TypeRegistry = require(script.Parent.Parent.Part.TypeRegistry)

local RandomizerWriter = {}

-- Per-rule write dispatch. Caller threads the rule from RandomizerRules.derive(...) so the
-- writer doesn't have to re-derive.
function RandomizerWriter.write(item, propKey, value, rule)
	if rule and rule.virtualEmitAttr then
		-- Item-level attribute; not in PartIcleProperties Configuration.
		pcall(function() item:SetAttribute(propKey, value) end)
		return
	end
	-- Native PE write  -  direct property assignment on the ParticleEmitter instance.
	-- PE has no Configuration child / TypeRegistry entry; props live as native
	-- ParticleEmitter members (Rate / Lifetime / Color / etc).
	if rule and rule.nativePE then
		local nativeOk = pcall(function() item[propKey] = value end)
		-- Clear stale Bezier handle JSON on the PE itself for graph rolls.
		-- Without this, GraphEditor._load() can resurrect the pre-randomize
		-- curve from the leftover handles instead of showing the new keypoints.
		if nativeOk and (rule.numberSequence or rule.colorSequence) then
			pcall(function() item:SetAttribute(propKey .. "_BezierHandles", nil) end)
		end
		return
	end
	-- stringForm rules (e.g. Trail Duration) store as a string; generator returns a number,
	-- writer tostring-wraps before TypeRegistry.write so the underlying string-attr accepts.
	local writeValue = value
	if rule and rule.stringForm and type(value) == "number" then
		writeValue = tostring(value)
	end
	-- TypeRegistry handles attrName overrides (BeamBrightness/PLRange/ImgFlipbookFramerate),
	-- nonNegative clamping, directAccess Trail native-property writes, and Configuration
	-- attribute writes for everything else. Wrapped in pcall so a single bad write doesn't
	-- abort a multi-prop Roll All.
	local writeOk = pcall(function() TypeRegistry.write(item, propKey, writeValue) end)

	-- Graph writes: clear stored Bezier handles ONLY after a successful TypeRegistry write.
	-- Otherwise a bad write would leave the prior valid graph in place but delete its handles.
	-- Handles attr is keyed by the LOGICAL prop key (matches the existing graph connector
	-- convention), not the attrName override.
	if writeOk and rule and (rule.numberSequence or rule.colorSequence) then
		-- Bezier handle attribute lives on the Configuration when one exists; on
		-- the item itself for raw ParticleEmitter / directAccess Trail.
		local target = TypeRegistry.getConfig(item) or item
		pcall(function() target:SetAttribute(propKey .. "_BezierHandles", nil) end)
	end
end

-- Convenience: write a batch of {[propKey] = {value, rule}} entries on one item. Useful for
-- the Randomize panel's apply path (Roll All -> snapshot per item -> writeBatch per item).
function RandomizerWriter.writeBatch(item, batch)
	for propKey, entry in pairs(batch) do
		RandomizerWriter.write(item, propKey, entry.value, entry.rule)
	end
end

return RandomizerWriter

children.name: Shortcuts
children.source:
--[[
	Shortcuts  -  Part-Icles V5 ShortcutKey System
	Copyright (C) 2026 Qwinkle

	Barrel for the ShortcutKey system. Submodules:
	  - Bindings: storage + validation. DEFAULTS / SUGGESTED both empty (fresh
	    installs start unbound, no Apply-Suggested). Rejects modifier-only key combos
	    (e.g. plain Ctrl), malformed combos, and unimplemented actionIds at load.
	    Bare non-modifier keys (plain "I", "`", function keys) ARE allowed.
	  - Wiring: factory (deps -> {open, close, isOpen, isCapturing, populate, reset,
	    getSettings, ensureSettings, setOnChanged}). Panel state machine + capture flow.
	  - Bootstrap: attach(deps) wires Settings panel "Shortcuts" button + panel close,
	    primes settings via ensureSettings, then starts Runtime.
	  - Runtime: start(deps) -> {stop}. UIS.InputBegan dispatcher with comboKey reverse-
	    index rebuilt on every save (via wiring.setOnChanged). Focus gates: wiring.isOpen
	    / wiring.isCapturing / GetFocusedTextBox. The `gameProcessedEvent` gate is NOT
	    used because Studio sets it true for nearly every keyboard event in Edit mode,
	    silencing all dispatch. Routes through Dispatcher for 50ms dedup +
	    `def.implemented==true` second guard.

	Disabled / not shipped:
	  - PluginAction registration for Studio Customize Shortcuts is DISABLED under the
	    P-prefix leader policy (see PluginActions.luau). Studio cannot prove the user
	    pressed our P leader before firing Triggered, so any Studio-bound chord would
	    end-run the policy. PluginActions.register stays as a no-op stub so Bootstrap
	    doesn't need to know. PluginAction instances created by older plugin versions
	    may still appear in the dialog with inert bindings  -  users can clear them via
	    Customize Shortcuts.
	  - Apply-Suggested panel affordance + SUGGESTED catalog are not shipped. New
	    installs start unbound; users explicitly Bind each action they want.

	Cmd/Win display preference (manual, not OS-detected): the Roblox plugin API exposes
	no host-OS detection, so Cmd-vs-Win labeling can't be auto-driven from the platform.
	The plugin reads an opt-in setting `DisplayCmdAsMeta` (boolean). Wiring re-reads it
	on open() so flips take effect next session. There is no visible panel toggle yet  - 
	Mac users flip it via the Studio dev console:
	  plugin:SetSetting("DisplayCmdAsMeta", true)

	NOT user-script-reachable. Internal-only.
]]

-- task.wait between requires so Luraph VM bootstrap of each obfuscated submodule
-- spreads across frames.
local Bindings  = require(script.Bindings); task.wait()
local Wiring    = require(script.Wiring); task.wait()
local Bootstrap = require(script.Bootstrap); task.wait()
-- Runtime.start(deps) wires the UIS dispatcher. Builds a comboKey reverse-index
-- from wiring.getSettings(), rebuilds on save via wiring.setOnChanged, gates
-- dispatch on isOpen/isCapturing/GetFocusedTextBox.
local Runtime   = require(script.Runtime); task.wait()
-- Disabled no-op stub under the P-leader policy  -  see PluginActions.luau header.
-- Bootstrap still calls register(); the call returns {stop = function() end}.
local PluginActions = require(script.PluginActions); task.wait()
-- Shared dispatch chokepoint. Currently only Runtime calls Dispatcher.dispatch.
-- Per-action + global 50ms dedup preserved as future-proofing for any new
-- dispatch path.
local Dispatcher = require(script.Dispatcher); task.wait()

return {
	Bindings = Bindings,
	Wiring = Wiring,
	Bootstrap = Bootstrap,
	Runtime = Runtime,
	PluginActions = PluginActions,
	Dispatcher = Dispatcher,
}

children.name: Bindings
children.source:
--[[
	Bindings  -  Part-Icles V5 ShortcutKey storage layer
	Copyright (C) 2026 Qwinkle

	Pure load / save / validate against the canonical plugin:GetSetting/SetSetting
	"Shortcuts" key (single key  -  avoids the period/backslash silent-failure issue
	from SetSetting).

	Storage shape:
	  {
	      version = 2,
	      overlayEnabled = true,
	      leaderKey = "P" | false,  -- KeyCode.Name string, or false for no leader
	      bindings = {
	          [actionId] = {key = "P", ctrl = true, alt = true, shift = false, meta = false},
	          ...
	      },
	  }

	`leaderKey` gates chord dispatch: when a string, that key must be held before any
	chord fires. When false, chords fire on direct keypress (no prefix). Default "P"
	preserves the historical hold-P UX for existing users.

	Combo is structured (key + 4 modifier bools) NOT a stringified "Ctrl+Shift+P".
	String display is rendering-only; storage stays structured so we can validate.

	DEFAULTS / SUGGESTED are both empty. New users start with everything unbound and
	explicitly Bind each action they want via the Shortcuts panel  -  pre-binding even
	a few actions amounts to surprise global behavior.

	load() also enforces `def.implemented == true`: a hand-edited or older settings
	entry that preserves a stub binding gets dropped at load time with a warn.
	Runtime safety must NOT trust UI filtering.

	NOT user-script-reachable. Internal-only.
]]

local Bindings = {}

-- v2 schema  -  load() detects v1-saved bindings still on the v1 defaults and clears
-- them so the user lands on the unbound starting state. Custom user chords are
-- preserved unchanged.
Bindings.VERSION = 2

-- v1-era default chords  -  closed set so the migration only touches users still on
-- the unmodified original install. List-of-entries form because a single actionId
-- has multiple historical default chords (Ctrl-era then P-leader-era). Migration
-- nils raw.bindings[actionId] when the saved combo matches ANY entry  -  covers
-- users from both install windows.
local OLD_DEFAULTS_V1 = {
	-- Ctrl-era defaults
	{actionId = "ToggleUI",         combo = {key = "P", ctrl = true,  alt = true,  shift = false, meta = false}},
	{actionId = "ToggleInventory",  combo = {key = "I", ctrl = true,  alt = false, shift = true,  meta = false}},
	{actionId = "ToggleProperties", combo = {key = "R", ctrl = true,  alt = false, shift = true,  meta = false}},
	-- P-leader-era defaults
	{actionId = "ToggleUI",         combo = {key = "P", ctrl = false, alt = false, shift = false, meta = false}},
	{actionId = "ToggleInventory",  combo = {key = "I", ctrl = false, alt = false, shift = false, meta = false}},
	{actionId = "ToggleProperties", combo = {key = "R", ctrl = false, alt = false, shift = false, meta = false}},
}

-- All shortcuts start unbound; the user explicitly assigns combos via the Bind
-- button. SUGGESTED is also empty  -  no per-row "Sug" affordance.
Bindings.DEFAULTS = {}
Bindings.SUGGESTED = {}

-- Reject keys that are *only* a modifier  -  modifier-without-non-modifier never reaches
-- a meaningful combo (would fire on plain Ctrl press). Capture-state UX rejects these too.
local MODIFIER_ONLY_KEYS = {
	LeftControl = true, RightControl = true, LeftAlt = true, RightAlt = true,
	LeftShift = true, RightShift = true, LeftMeta = true, RightMeta = true,
	LeftSuper = true, RightSuper = true,
}

-- Default leader; existing users land here on first load after the v39.203 schema
-- extension so behavior is unchanged from prior versions.
Bindings.DEFAULT_LEADER = "P"

-- Resolve the configured leader from a settings table. Returns:
--   string  - the KeyCode.Name leader must be held to dispatch chords.
--   false   - no leader; chord dispatches on direct keypress.
function Bindings.getLeaderKey(settings)
	if type(settings) ~= "table" then return Bindings.DEFAULT_LEADER end
	local lk = settings.leaderKey
	if lk == false then return false end
	if type(lk) == "string" and lk ~= "" then return lk end
	return Bindings.DEFAULT_LEADER
end

-- Validate a leader string against Enum.KeyCode + modifier-only blocklist.
-- Returns the cleaned leader (string or false) and a bool indicating whether
-- the input was valid. Callers fall back to DEFAULT_LEADER on invalid input.
function Bindings.isValidLeader(lk)
	if lk == false then return false, true end
	if type(lk) ~= "string" or lk == "" then return nil, false end
	if MODIFIER_ONLY_KEYS[lk] then return nil, false end
	local ok, kc = pcall(function() return Enum.KeyCode[lk] end)
	if not ok or kc == nil then return nil, false end
	return lk, true
end

function Bindings.isValidCombo(combo)
	if type(combo) ~= "table" then return false end
	if type(combo.key) ~= "string" or combo.key == "" then return false end
	if type(combo.ctrl) ~= "boolean" then return false end
	if type(combo.alt) ~= "boolean" then return false end
	if type(combo.shift) ~= "boolean" then return false end
	if type(combo.meta) ~= "boolean" then return false end
	if MODIFIER_ONLY_KEYS[combo.key] then return false end
	-- Bare-key bindings (e.g. plain "I" or "`") MUST work. We don't require ≥1
	-- modifier as a UX guardrail  -  if a user binds a viewport key and regrets it,
	-- they can rebind/unbind via the panel.
	-- KeyCode validation: if Enum.KeyCode[combo.key] doesn't resolve, reject. pcall the
	-- Enum index because Roblox Studio raises rather than returning nil on unknown names.
	local ok, kc = pcall(function() return Enum.KeyCode[combo.key] end)
	if not ok or kc == nil then return false end
	return true
end

-- Stable comma-joined modifier-prefixed key string. Used as a hash for collision detection
-- on load AND in capture flow. Modifier order is fixed (ctrl,alt,shift,meta) so two combos
-- with the same logical modifiers + key always produce the same comboKey.
function Bindings.comboKey(combo)
	return string.format("%s+%s+%s+%s+%s",
		combo.ctrl and "C" or "_",
		combo.alt  and "A" or "_",
		combo.shift and "S" or "_",
		combo.meta and "M" or "_",
		combo.key)
end

-- Pretty-print combo with leader prefix. Examples: "P + I", "T + Shift+T", "Ctrl+I"
-- (no leader). Storage stays as second-key chord; leader prepended at display time so
-- users see the full sequence at a glance. `leader` is the configured leader string,
-- or false for no leader.
function Bindings.formatCombo(combo, isMac, leader)
	if not combo then return "(unbound)" end
	local parts = {}
	if combo.ctrl then table.insert(parts, "Ctrl") end
	if combo.alt then table.insert(parts, "Alt") end
	if combo.shift then table.insert(parts, "Shift") end
	if combo.meta then table.insert(parts, isMac and "Cmd" or "Win") end
	table.insert(parts, combo.key)
	local chord = table.concat(parts, "+")
	if leader == false then return chord end
	local lk = (type(leader) == "string" and leader ~= "") and leader or Bindings.DEFAULT_LEADER
	return lk .. " + " .. chord
end

-- Load + validate against the current ActionCatalog. Cases:
-- 1. Setting missing → empty bindings (DEFAULTS is empty).
-- 2. version mismatch (newer): warn + return empty bindings, don't overwrite stored setting.
-- 3. version older (no version OR <2): run migrations before validation  - 
--    TogglePlugin->ToggleUI rename, then v1 default-chord clear.
-- 4. binding for unknown actionId: skip + warn once.
-- 5. malformed binding: skip + warn.
-- 6. duplicate combo: alphabetical-actionId wins, others dropped + warn.
-- Returns: settings table {version, overlayEnabled, bindings}.
function Bindings.load(plugin, ActionCatalog)
	local raw = plugin:GetSetting("Shortcuts")
	if type(raw) ~= "table" then
		return {version = Bindings.VERSION, overlayEnabled = true, leaderKey = Bindings.DEFAULT_LEADER, bindings = Bindings._copyDefaults()}
	end
	-- Normalize raw.version to a finite number before any comparison. Corrupt or
	-- hand-edited settings can leave it as a string, table, or NaN  -  direct
	-- comparison would throw and abort shortcut bootstrap.
	local rawVersion = tonumber(raw.version)
	if rawVersion ~= rawVersion then rawVersion = nil end -- NaN guard
	if rawVersion and rawVersion > Bindings.VERSION then
		warn("[Part-Icles Shortcuts] settings version unsupported (saved="..tostring(raw.version)..", current="..Bindings.VERSION.."); using defaults")
		return {version = Bindings.VERSION, overlayEnabled = true, leaderKey = Bindings.DEFAULT_LEADER, bindings = Bindings._copyDefaults()}
	end
	-- TogglePlugin renamed to ToggleUI. Soft migration  -  if a saved binding still uses
	-- the old key, transfer it to the new key so the user's chord survives the rename.
	-- Done before validation so the migrated entry runs through the same checks.
	if type(raw.bindings) == "table" and raw.bindings.TogglePlugin and not raw.bindings.ToggleUI then
		raw.bindings.ToggleUI = raw.bindings.TogglePlugin
		raw.bindings.TogglePlugin = nil
	end
	-- ToggleAnimateLoop retired in favor of ToggleEnable (auto-routes to AnimateLoop
	-- in Animate mode, Enabled in Emit mode). Move the saved chord to ToggleEnable
	-- when free; otherwise drop with a warning.
	if type(raw.bindings) == "table" and raw.bindings.ToggleAnimateLoop then
		if not raw.bindings.ToggleEnable then
			raw.bindings.ToggleEnable = raw.bindings.ToggleAnimateLoop
		else
			warn("[Part-Icles Shortcuts] ToggleAnimateLoop binding dropped  -  ToggleEnable already bound (which now covers both modes)")
		end
		raw.bindings.ToggleAnimateLoop = nil
	end
	-- v1 -> v2 migration. v2 has no DEFAULTS  -  all bindings start unbound. So the
	-- migration just NILS bindings still on the v1 default chord; user-customized
	-- chords pass through unchanged.
	if type(raw.bindings) == "table" and (not rawVersion or rawVersion < 2) then
		for _, entry in ipairs(OLD_DEFAULTS_V1) do
			local current = raw.bindings[entry.actionId]
			if current and Bindings.isValidCombo(current) and Bindings.comboKey(current) == Bindings.comboKey(entry.combo) then
				raw.bindings[entry.actionId] = nil
			end
		end
	end
	local validated = {}
	if type(raw.bindings) == "table" then
		for actionId, combo in pairs(raw.bindings) do
			local def = ActionCatalog[actionId]
			if not def then
				warn(("[Part-Icles Shortcuts] binding for unknown action %q ignored; remove via Settings panel"):format(actionId))
			elseif def.implemented ~= true then
				-- Stubs (ResetSelection / OpenGraphEditor / OpenColorPicker) must not be
				-- dispatchable from the keyboard even if a hand-edited settings entry
				-- preserves them. Panel UI filters them too, but runtime safety must
				-- NOT trust UI filtering  -  refuse here.
				warn(("[Part-Icles Shortcuts] binding for unimplemented action %q dropped; rebind via the Settings panel once it ships"):format(actionId))
			elseif not Bindings.isValidCombo(combo) then
				warn(("[Part-Icles Shortcuts] binding for %q is malformed; falling back to unbound"):format(actionId))
			else
				validated[actionId] = combo
			end
		end
	end
	-- Pass 2: deterministic duplicate-combo handling. Alphabetical actionId wins.
	local sorted = {}
	for actionId in pairs(validated) do table.insert(sorted, actionId) end
	table.sort(sorted)
	local seenCombos = {}
	local final = {}
	for _, actionId in ipairs(sorted) do
		local combo = validated[actionId]
		local k = Bindings.comboKey(combo)
		if seenCombos[k] then
			warn(("[Part-Icles Shortcuts] duplicate combo on load: %q wins over %q"):format(seenCombos[k], actionId))
		else
			seenCombos[k] = actionId
			final[actionId] = combo
		end
	end
	-- Force overlayEnabled true on every load. There's no UI to flip it back, and a
	-- stale build or hand-edited setting could leave it false → Runtime would bail
	-- silently. If a future settings UI exposes this toggle, restore raw.overlayEnabled.
	local overlayEnabled = true
	-- Leader: accept string KeyCode.Name, false (no leader), or fall back to default.
	-- Hand-edited / corrupt entries land on the default with a warning.
	local leaderClean, leaderOk = Bindings.isValidLeader(raw.leaderKey)
	if raw.leaderKey ~= nil and not leaderOk then
		warn(("[Part-Icles Shortcuts] invalid leaderKey %q; using default %q"):format(tostring(raw.leaderKey), Bindings.DEFAULT_LEADER))
	end
	if raw.leaderKey == nil then leaderClean = Bindings.DEFAULT_LEADER end
	if leaderClean == nil then leaderClean = Bindings.DEFAULT_LEADER end
	local result = {version = Bindings.VERSION, overlayEnabled = overlayEnabled, leaderKey = leaderClean, bindings = final}
	-- Persist post-migration state so subsequent loads find raw.version == VERSION
	-- and skip the migration block. Otherwise the migration replays each session.
	if rawVersion ~= Bindings.VERSION then
		pcall(Bindings.save, plugin, result)
	end
	return result
end

function Bindings.save(plugin, settings)
	local leader = Bindings.getLeaderKey(settings)
	plugin:SetSetting("Shortcuts", {
		version = Bindings.VERSION,
		overlayEnabled = settings.overlayEnabled ~= false,
		leaderKey = leader,
		bindings = settings.bindings or {},
	})
end

function Bindings._copyDefaults()
	local out = {}
	for k, v in pairs(Bindings.DEFAULTS) do
		out[k] = {key = v.key, ctrl = v.ctrl, alt = v.alt, shift = v.shift, meta = v.meta}
	end
	return out
end

-- Find which actionId currently owns the given combo, or nil. O(n) over bindings  - 
-- bindings table is bounded by ActionCatalog size (~15) so this is fine on every capture.
function Bindings.findOwner(settings, combo)
	if not Bindings.isValidCombo(combo) then return nil end
	local target = Bindings.comboKey(combo)
	for actionId, existing in pairs(settings.bindings or {}) do
		if Bindings.comboKey(existing) == target then return actionId end
	end
	return nil
end

return Bindings

children.name: Bootstrap
children.source:
--[[
	Bootstrap  -  Part-Icles V5 ShortcutKey wiring entry point
	Copyright (C) 2026 Qwinkle

	Mirrors Randomizer/Bootstrap.luau.

	Order of operations:
	  1. Build ShortcutsWiring state machine, register ctx.ShortcutsWiring.
	  2. wiring.ensureSettings()  -  primes _settings with the user's saved bindings
	     (or empty on a fresh install) BEFORE Runtime.start, so the dispatcher's
	     first index rebuild has data.
	  3. Shortcuts.Runtime.start  -  UIS dispatcher hooks wiring.setOnChanged for live
	     index rebuilds; registers via ConnectionManager so plugin teardown disconnects
	     cleanly.
	  4. Settings panel "Shortcuts" button → toggle wiring.open/close.
	  5. Panel headerCloseBtn (built-in W.makeToolPanel Hd.Close) → close().

	Required deps shape:
	  ctx (must contain ctx.plugin + ctx.Actions),
	  UI (must contain ShortcutPanel + ShortcutsList + ShortcutsSearch + ShortcutsReset
	      + ShortcutsHeaderClose + ShortcutsButton on Settings panel),
	  Connections (ConnectionManager  -  same instance used by init.server.lua),
	  Shortcuts (the barrel; needs Bindings + Wiring + Runtime),
	  Widgets, Theme.
]]

local Bootstrap = {}

function Bootstrap.attach(deps)
	local ctx = deps.ctx
	local UI = deps.UI
	local Connections = deps.Connections
	local Shortcuts = deps.Shortcuts

	local wiring = Shortcuts.Wiring({
		ctx = ctx,
		panel = {
			panel = UI.ShortcutPanel,
			scrollList = UI.ShortcutsList,
			searchBox = UI.ShortcutsSearch,
			resetBtn = UI.ShortcutsReset,
			headerCloseBtn = UI.ShortcutsHeaderClose,
			leaderLabel = UI.ShortcutsLeaderLabel,
			leaderSetBtn = UI.ShortcutsLeaderSet,
			leaderClearBtn = UI.ShortcutsLeaderClear,
		},
		Bindings = Shortcuts.Bindings,
		-- Forward Connections so search/reset signals register through the shared
		-- ConnectionManager (consistent with every other top-level wiring path).
		Connections = Connections,
		Widgets = deps.Widgets,
		Theme = deps.Theme,
	})
	ctx.ShortcutsWiring = wiring

	-- Prime _settings at setup so the runtime (which attaches below) sees the user's
	-- saved bindings (or empty fresh install) on first dispatch.
	wiring.ensureSettings()

	-- Shared dispatcher with 50ms dedup. Runtime is currently the only live caller  - 
	-- dedup is retained as future-proofing for any new dispatch path that gets added.
	-- Built BEFORE Runtime.start so it can hook in.
	local dispatcher = Shortcuts.Dispatcher.create(ctx)
	ctx.ShortcutsDispatcher = dispatcher

	-- Start the UIS dispatcher. wiring.setOnChanged is hooked inside Runtime.start so
	-- any save-side rebuild flows through. ctx.ShortcutsRuntime exposed for teardown
	-- (plugin Unloading -> stop()) and future debug introspection.
	local runtime = Shortcuts.Runtime.start({
		ctx = ctx,
		wiring = wiring,
		Bindings = Shortcuts.Bindings,
		Connections = Connections,
		dispatcher = dispatcher,
	})
	ctx.ShortcutsRuntime = runtime

	-- PluginActions.register is a disabled no-op under the P-prefix leader policy.
	-- The call is kept (returns {stop = function() end}) so we don't have to wire
	-- conditional code paths if the policy ever flips back. See PluginActions.luau
	-- header for the bypass rationale.
	if ctx.plugin then
		ctx.ShortcutsPluginActions = Shortcuts.PluginActions.register(ctx.plugin, ctx, wiring, dispatcher)
	end

	-- Settings panel "Shortcuts" button. Toggle behaviour: open if closed, close if open.
	if UI.ShortcutsButton then
		Connections["ShortcutsToggle"] = UI.ShortcutsButton.Activated:Connect(function()
			if wiring.isOpen() then wiring.close() else wiring.open() end
		end)
	end

	-- Built-in W.makeToolPanel header X. close() so capture connection tears down.
	if UI.ShortcutsHeaderClose then
		Connections["ShortcutsHeaderClose"] = UI.ShortcutsHeaderClose.Activated:Connect(function()
			wiring.close()
		end)
	end

	return wiring
end

return Bootstrap

children.name: Dispatcher
children.source:
--[[
	Dispatcher  -  Part-Icles V5 ShortcutKey shared dispatch
	Copyright (C) 2026 Qwinkle

	The only live dispatch path is `UIS InputBegan -> Runtime overlay reverse-index
	match -> handler`. Single dispatch chokepoint is preserved as future-proofing:
	any new path that gets added calls `Dispatcher.dispatch(actionId)` and inherits
	the 50ms dedup discipline.

	Two dedup layers  -  kept because Runtime can still fire twice if an InputBegan
	repeat slips through the focus gates:
	  - `_lastFire[actionId] -> os.clock()` per-action 50ms window. Catches same-action
	    double dispatch.
	  - `_lastAnyFire -> os.clock()` global 50ms window. Catches cross-action collisions
	     -  future-proofing for any additional dispatch path.

	The `def.implemented == true` guard also runs here so callers can drop their own
	duplicate checks (kept defensively at the caller in case dispatcher is bypassed).

	Lifecycle:
	  Dispatcher.create(ctx) returns `{dispatch}`. Stored on `ctx.ShortcutsDispatcher`
	  by Bootstrap. No teardown needed  -  `_lastFire` + `_lastAnyFire` are scoped per
	  Dispatcher instance and GC'd when ctx is dropped.

	NOT user-script-reachable. Internal-only.
]]

local Dispatcher = {}

local DEDUP_WINDOW = 0.05  -- 50ms; matches Runtime's prior per-instance dedup

function Dispatcher.create(ctx)
	local self = {}
	local _lastFire = {}      -- per-actionId: same chord on overlay+Studio doesn't double-fire.
	-- Initialize to nil + guarded check so the very first dispatch in a fresh context
	-- isn't suppressed when os.clock() happens to be below DEDUP_WINDOW. Could also
	-- use -math.huge; nil reads cleaner.
	local _lastAnyFire = nil  -- global cross-action dedup window.

	function self.dispatch(actionId)
		if type(actionId) ~= "string" or actionId == "" then return end
		local Actions = ctx.Actions
		local def = Actions and Actions[actionId]
		-- Second-guard applied centrally: even if a caller bypasses its own implemented
		-- check, the dispatcher refuses stub actions.
		if not def or def.implemented ~= true then return end
		local now = os.clock()
		local last = _lastFire[actionId]
		if last and (now - last) < DEDUP_WINDOW then return end
		if _lastAnyFire and (now - _lastAnyFire) < DEDUP_WINDOW then return end
		_lastFire[actionId] = now
		_lastAnyFire = now
		local ok, err = pcall(def.handler, ctx)
		if not ok then
			warn(("[Part-Icles Shortcuts] handler error for %q: %s"):format(actionId, tostring(err)))
		end
	end

	return self
end

return Dispatcher

children.name: PluginActions
children.source:
--[[
	PluginActions  -  DISABLED under the P-prefix leader policy
	Copyright (C) 2026 Qwinkle

	Empty stub. Studio `PluginAction` registration was the original mechanism for
	surfacing plugin shortcuts in Studio's File → Advanced → Customize Shortcuts
	dialog. The hold-P leader policy ("all keybinds require P first") makes that
	mechanism unsafe because Studio cannot prove the user pressed our leader key
	before firing `PluginAction.Triggered`  -  Studio-bound chords would end-run the
	policy.

	The previous body created `PluginAction`s with `allowBinding = true` and hooked
	their `Triggered` signal through the shared dispatcher. That entire path is
	deliberately deleted here so a future careless edit cannot re-enable the bypass
	by calling a "legacy" function. The stub keeps the same call signature so
	Bootstrap doesn't have to know whether the policy is active.

	Side effect: `PluginAction` instances created by older plugin versions may still
	appear in Studio's Customize Shortcuts dialog with stale bindings. Those bindings
	cannot fire because we no longer connect Triggered. Users can clear them via the
	dialog at their leisure  -  the plugin cannot mutate Studio's binding store.

	NOT user-script-reachable. Internal-only.
]]

local PluginActions = {}

function PluginActions.register(_plugin, _ctx, _wiring, _dispatcher)
	return {stop = function() end}
end

return PluginActions

children.name: Runtime
children.source:
--[[
	Runtime  -  Part-Icles V5 ShortcutKey UIS dispatch
	Copyright (C) 2026 Qwinkle

	Connects keyboard chords to ActionCatalog handlers via a comboKey reverse-index
	built from `wiring.getSettings()`.

	**Hold-P leader:**
	All shortcuts require P held down at the moment of the chord keypress. Roblox
	Studio uses heavy modifier prefixes (Ctrl/Shift/Alt) for its own shortcuts, so a
	dedicated leader key sidesteps that whole conflict surface. Hold-style (vs.
	tap-once + 1s window) lets the user hold P and tap multiple keys to fire several
	actions in a row without re-pressing P each time.

	Sequence:
	  1. User holds P down. P alone fires nothing (P is the modifier, not an action).
	  2. While P is still held, any other keypress builds a combo and dispatches if
	     its comboKey hits the reverse-index. User can tap several chord keys in
	     succession.
	  3. User releases P → leader off. Next chord key without P held is ignored.

	Architecture:
	  - Reverse-index `_index[comboKey] -> actionId` rebuilt on demand AND whenever
	    the Wiring layer fires its onChanged callback (after every save: commit /
	    unbind / reset).
	  - 50ms per-actionId dedup + global cross-action dedup live in
	    Shortcuts.Dispatcher.
	  - Focus gating:
	      1. `wiring.isCapturing()` → skip (panel actively capturing a chord).
	      2. `UserInputService:GetFocusedTextBox()` → skip (let typing pass through
	         to the focused text input  -  overlay shortcuts must NOT eat keystrokes
	         from properties / search / config inputs).
	      3. `wiring.isOpen()` → SUPPRESS but allow `ToggleShortcuts` and `ToggleUI`
	         through: the same shortcut that opened the panel must be able to close
	         it, and ToggleUI must work when the panel is open under a hidden
	         ScreenGui. Other actions are blocked so chord-tapping during binding
	         doesn't fire random actions.
	    The `gameProcessedEvent` gate is intentionally NOT used because Studio sets
	    it true for nearly every keyboard event.

	Required deps shape:
	  ctx (must contain ctx.Actions),
	  wiring (needs getSettings + isOpen + isCapturing + setOnChanged),
	  Bindings (for comboKey + isValidCombo),
	  Connections (ConnectionManager),
	  dispatcher (Shortcuts.Dispatcher.create(ctx)).

	NOT user-script-reachable. Internal-only.
]]

local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")

-- Leader is now user-configurable via Settings (Bindings.leaderKey). Defaults to P
-- so existing users see no behavior change on upgrade. A leader of `false` skips
-- the gate entirely; chord combos fire on direct keypress.
local DEFAULT_LEADER_KEYCODE = Enum.KeyCode.P

local Runtime = {}

function Runtime.start(deps)
	local ctx = deps.ctx
	local wiring = deps.wiring
	local Bindings = deps.Bindings
	local Connections = deps.Connections
	local dispatcher = deps.dispatcher

	local runtime = {}
	local _index = {}        -- comboKey -> actionId

	function runtime._rebuildIndex()
		_index = {}
		local settings = wiring.getSettings()
		if not settings or settings.overlayEnabled == false then return end
		local Actions = ctx.Actions
		for actionId, combo in pairs(settings.bindings or {}) do
			local def = Actions and Actions[actionId]
			-- Index-build filter: stubs skipped here so a malformed config doesn't
			-- even land in _index. Dispatcher repeats the check defensively at fire
			-- time in case bypass paths land.
			if def and def.implemented == true and Bindings.isValidCombo(combo) then
				_index[Bindings.comboKey(combo)] = actionId
			end
		end
	end

	-- Build a combo table from a keyboard InputObject. Mirrors Wiring's capture-side combo
	-- construction so the comboKey hash matches between save-time and dispatch-time.
	local function _buildComboFromInput(input)
		local combo = {
			key = input.KeyCode.Name,
			ctrl = UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.LeftControl) or UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.RightControl),
			alt = UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.LeftAlt) or UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.RightAlt),
			shift = UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.LeftShift) or UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.RightShift),
			meta = false,
		}
		pcall(function()
			combo.meta = UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.LeftMeta) or UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.RightMeta)
		end)
		return combo
	end

	-- Resolve the live leader KeyCode from settings on each check. Settings table is
	-- in-memory after first ensureSettings, so the lookup is cheap. Returns the
	-- KeyCode enum value OR nil when leader is disabled (false in settings).
	local function _currentLeaderKeyCode()
		local settings = wiring.getSettings()
		local lk = Bindings.getLeaderKey(settings)
		if lk == false then return nil end
		local ok, kc = pcall(function() return Enum.KeyCode[lk] end)
		if ok and kc then return kc end
		return DEFAULT_LEADER_KEYCODE
	end

	-- Hold-leader: dispatch fires on any second-key press WHILE the leader is held.
	-- Lets the user hold the leader and tap multiple keys to toggle several actions
	-- in a row without re-arming each time. When leader is disabled (settings.leaderKey
	-- == false), this returns true unconditionally so chords fire on direct keypress.
	local function _isLeaderHeld()
		local kc = _currentLeaderKeyCode()
		if kc == nil then return true end
		return UserInputService:IsKeyDown(kc)
	end

	local function _dispatchActionId(actionId)
		if not actionId then return end
		if dispatcher then
			dispatcher.dispatch(actionId)
			return
		end
		-- Defensive fallback if Bootstrap forgot to wire dispatcher.
		warn("[Part-Icles Shortcuts] Runtime built without dispatcher; firing direct (dedup absent)")
		local def = ctx.Actions and ctx.Actions[actionId]
		if def and def.implemented == true then
			local ok, err = pcall(def.handler, ctx)
			if not ok then
				warn(("[Part-Icles Shortcuts] handler error for %q: %s"):format(actionId, tostring(err)))
			end
		end
	end

	function runtime._onInputBegan(input, _gameProcessedEvent)
		if input.UserInputType ~= Enum.UserInputType.Keyboard then return end
		-- Focus gates. gameProcessedEvent intentionally unused  -  see header comment.
		if wiring.isCapturing and wiring.isCapturing() then return end
		if UserInputService:GetFocusedTextBox() then return end

		-- Hold-leader: leader held + any other key press = dispatch. Pressing the
		-- leader alone does nothing (it's the modifier, not an action). When the
		-- leader is disabled (settings.leaderKey == false), no key is reserved and
		-- the held-check passes unconditionally so any chord keypress dispatches.
		local leaderKC = _currentLeaderKeyCode()
		if leaderKC and input.KeyCode == leaderKC then return end
		if not _isLeaderHeld() then return end
		local combo = _buildComboFromInput(input)
		if not Bindings.isValidCombo(combo) then return end
		local actionId = _index[Bindings.comboKey(combo)]
		if not actionId then return end
		-- When the Shortcuts panel itself is open, only ToggleShortcuts can dispatch  - 
		-- that lets the same shortcut close the panel it just opened. Other actions
		-- are suppressed so chord-tapping inside the panel doesn't accidentally fire
		-- random actions while the user is binding. ToggleUI is also allowlisted so
		-- the user can recover when the panel is open under a hidden ScreenGui
		-- (panel.Visible=true but parent disabled).
		if wiring.isOpen() and actionId ~= "ToggleShortcuts" and actionId ~= "ToggleUI" then return end
		_dispatchActionId(actionId)
	end

	-- Build the index now (Bootstrap calls ensureSettings before us so getSettings returns
	-- a populated table). Hook onChanged so future saves rebuild.
	runtime._rebuildIndex()
	wiring.setOnChanged(runtime._rebuildIndex)

	local conn = UserInputService.InputBegan:Connect(runtime._onInputBegan)
	if Connections then
		Connections["ShortcutsRuntime"] = conn
	end

	function runtime.stop()
		if conn then conn:Disconnect(); conn = nil end
		wiring.setOnChanged(nil)
		_index = {}
	end

	return runtime
end

return Runtime

children.name: Wiring
children.source:
--[[
	Wiring  -  Part-Icles V5 ShortcutKey panel state machine
	Copyright (C) 2026 Qwinkle

	Factory: `(deps) -> {open, close, isOpen, populate, ...}`.

	State machine:
	  - Closed: panel.Visible = false. _settings table is the in-memory truth.
	  - Open: visible. populate() rebuilds rows from ctx.Actions filtered by
	    `def.implemented==true`. Search box re-filters live via
	    :GetPropertyChangedSignal("Text").
	  - Capturing: a row's Bind button was clicked. _captureActionId is set, all
	    input is intercepted by the active UIS connection until either (a) Esc
	    cancels, (b) a valid non-modifier-only key fires (with or without
	    modifiers), or (c) any other Bind button is clicked (capture handoff  - 
	    mirrors Studio's keybind UX).

	Save flow (Capture commit):
	  1. New combo built from UIS state.
	  2. Bindings.findOwner(settings, combo) → if a different action owns it,
	     warn + drop the previous binding. Conflict policy is "simple override".
	  3. _settings.bindings[actionId] = combo. Bindings.save(plugin, _settings).
	  4. populate() rebuilds rows so combo display refreshes for both winner +
	     previous owner.

	Reset:
	  - Two-click confirm. First click flips resetBtn.Text to "Click again to
	    confirm", arms _resetArmed + _resetArmedAt. Second click within
	    _resetConfirmWindow seconds → mod.reset() (Bindings._copyDefaults() into
	    _settings.bindings, save, populate). No second click → task.delay restores
	    label after window. close() also disarms.

	Settings priming:
	  - mod.ensureSettings() lazy-loads Bindings.load(plugin, Actions) on first
	    access.
	  - Bootstrap calls ensureSettings() right after construction so the runtime
	    (which attaches before any user opens the panel) sees the user's saved
	    bindings on first dispatch.
	  - getSettings() routes through ensureSettings() so it never returns nil.

	NOT user-script-reachable. Internal-only.

	Required deps shape:
	  ctx (must contain ctx.plugin + ctx.Actions),
	  panel = {panel, scrollList, searchBox, resetBtn, headerCloseBtn},
	  Bindings (the storage submodule),
	  Connections (ConnectionManager  -  registers searchBox/resetBtn signals so
	    plugin teardown disconnects them, consistent with every other top-level
	    wiring path),
	  Widgets, Theme.
]]

local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")

return function(deps)
	local ctx = deps.ctx
	local plugin = ctx.plugin
	local Actions = ctx.Actions
	local panel = deps.panel.panel
	local scrollList = deps.panel.scrollList
	local searchBox = deps.panel.searchBox
	local resetBtn = deps.panel.resetBtn
	local leaderLabel = deps.panel.leaderLabel
	local leaderSetBtn = deps.panel.leaderSetBtn
	local leaderClearBtn = deps.panel.leaderClearBtn
	local Bindings = deps.Bindings
	local Widgets = deps.Widgets
	local Theme = deps.Theme
	local Connections = deps.Connections  -- register signal connections through ConnectionManager

	local W = Widgets
	local T = Theme
	local mod = {}

	local _settings  -- {version, overlayEnabled, bindings}
	local _open = false
	local _captureActionId = nil
	local _captureConn = nil
	-- Forward-declared so _startCapture's mutual-exclusion block can see these as
	-- upvalues. Initialized in the Leader-capture section further down.
	local _leaderCapturing = false
	local _leaderCaptureConn = nil
	local _rows = {}  -- {actionId -> {frame, comboLabel, bindBtn, unbindBtn, applyBtn}}
	local _conflictTimer = nil
	local _destroyed = false
	-- Runtime rebuilds its comboKey reverse-index when bindings change. _onChanged is a
	-- single-callback hook (Runtime.start sets this); fired from every save path (commit
	-- / unbind / reset). Single consumer, so no full Signal needed.
	local _onChanged = nil
	local function _fireChanged()
		if _onChanged then pcall(_onChanged) end
	end
	-- Manual Cmd/Win display preference (NOT OS detection). Roblox plugin API has no
	-- host-OS hook, so Mac vs Win meta-key labeling can't be auto-driven. We read the
	-- plugin setting `DisplayCmdAsMeta` (boolean) at open time; Mac users flip via
	-- `plugin:SetSetting("DisplayCmdAsMeta", true)` in the Studio dev console. Display
	-- labels render "Cmd+" instead of "Win+" for combos with meta=true. open() refreshes
	-- per session so a flip + reopen reflects the label preference immediately. There is
	-- no visible panel toggle yet  -  could surface as a checkbox near Reset if Mac uptake
	-- creates demand.
	local _isMac = false
	local function _refreshIsMac()
		local v = plugin:GetSetting("DisplayCmdAsMeta")
		_isMac = (type(v) == "boolean") and v or false
	end

	-- =========================================================
	-- Capture flow
	-- =========================================================

	local function _stopCapture(reason)
		if _captureConn then _captureConn:Disconnect(); _captureConn = nil end
		_captureActionId = nil
		-- Restore button labels (populate rebuilds, simpler than per-row state restore).
		mod.populate()
	end

	-- Transient conflict notice {actionId, expiresAt, message}. Populate displays
	-- the message on the affected row's combo label in red until expiresAt.
	local _conflictNotice = nil

	local function _commitCombo(actionId, combo)
		-- _commitCombo can fire with actionId == nil under a race between _stopCapture's
		-- _captureActionId clear and an in-flight InputBegan event. Bail early so format/
		-- warn/save calls never receive nil. The capture flow's caller already gates
		-- re-firing on the boolean return (false → don't _stopCapture again).
		if type(actionId) ~= "string" or actionId == "" then return false end
		if not Bindings.isValidCombo(combo) then return false end
		mod.ensureSettings()
		local owner = Bindings.findOwner(_settings, combo)
		if owner and owner ~= actionId then
			warn(("[Part-Icles Shortcuts] %s overrides previous binding %s -> %s"):format(
				tostring(actionId), tostring(owner), Bindings.formatCombo(combo, _isMac, Bindings.getLeaderKey(_settings))))
			_settings.bindings[owner] = nil
			-- Stash a transient notice for the row that just lost its binding.
			-- Populate (called from _fireChanged below) will overlay it; another
			-- populate runs after 3s to clear.
			local newName = (Actions[actionId] and Actions[actionId].displayName) or actionId
			_conflictNotice = {
				actionId = owner,
				expiresAt = os.clock() + 3,
				message = "Reassigned to " .. newName,
			}
			if _conflictTimer then pcall(task.cancel, _conflictTimer); _conflictTimer = nil end
			_conflictTimer = task.delay(3, function()
				_conflictTimer = nil
				if _destroyed then return end
				if _conflictNotice and _conflictNotice.actionId == owner then
					_conflictNotice = nil
					mod.populate()
				end
			end)
		end
		_settings.bindings[actionId] = combo
		Bindings.save(plugin, _settings)
		_fireChanged()
		return true
	end

	local function _startCapture(actionId)
		-- Tear down any existing capture before arming a new one  -  regardless of
		-- whether actionId matches. Otherwise same-row double-click would orphan
		-- the prior listener with its stale captured actionId still alive.
		if _captureConn then _stopCapture("rearm") end
		-- Mutual exclusion with leader capture (defined later in this file). The
		-- next keypress must commit as a chord, not as a new leader. Forward-decl
		-- via _leaderCaptureConn upvalue  -  closure resolves at fire time.
		if _leaderCaptureConn then
			_leaderCaptureConn:Disconnect()
			_leaderCaptureConn = nil
			_leaderCapturing = false
			-- Label refresh happens inline since the leader-row helper isn't visible
			-- to this closure yet. Safe because populate() runs at the end of any
			-- commit path that follows.
			if leaderLabel then
				local lk = Bindings.getLeaderKey(_settings)
				leaderLabel.Text = lk == false and "Leader: (none)" or ("Leader: " .. tostring(lk))
				leaderLabel.TextColor3 = lk == false and T.MutedGold or T.BrightGold
			end
		end
		_captureActionId = actionId
		local row = _rows[actionId]
		if row and row.comboLabel then
			local leaderName = Bindings.getLeaderKey(_settings)
			local hint = leaderName == false
				and "Press key... (Esc cancels)"
				or ("Press key... (hold "..tostring(leaderName).." + key; Esc cancels)")
			row.comboLabel.Text = hint
		end
		-- Bind the actionId in the closure rather than reading the _captureActionId
		-- upvalue at fire time. Otherwise an InputBegan event in flight when
		-- _stopCapture nils the upvalue would pass nil to _commitCombo. Closure
		-- capture pins the value at _startCapture time; _stopCapture's Disconnect
		-- kills the listener but the bound `actionId` survives until that happens.
		local capturingActionId = actionId
		-- InputBegan listener. ProcessEvent passes through Studio bindings  -  we want even
		-- captured-by-Studio combos to commit here, so we listen on InputBegan and check
		-- modifiers via UIS:IsKeyDown rather than relying on the InputObject having them.
		_captureConn = UserInputService.InputBegan:Connect(function(input)
			if input.UserInputType ~= Enum.UserInputType.Keyboard then return end
			-- Bail when a TextBox is focused so typing in the Shortcuts search (or
			-- any other plugin TextBox) doesn't get captured as a chord. Escape is
			-- the exception  -  letting it through lets the user cancel capture
			-- without un-focusing first.
			if input.KeyCode == Enum.KeyCode.Escape then _stopCapture("escape"); return end
			if UserInputService:GetFocusedTextBox() then return end
			-- Leader never lands as the chord key. With hold-leader semantics the user
			-- holds the leader first then taps the chord key; capture must ignore the
			-- leader press so it doesn't bind the leader as the second key. When the
			-- leader is disabled (leaderKey == false), no key is reserved.
			local leaderName = Bindings.getLeaderKey(_settings)
			if leaderName ~= false and input.KeyCode.Name == leaderName then return end
			local kcName = input.KeyCode.Name
			-- Reject modifier-only press; wait for the chord-finishing non-modifier.
			local combo = {
				key = kcName,
				ctrl = UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.LeftControl) or UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.RightControl),
				alt = UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.LeftAlt) or UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.RightAlt),
				shift = UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.LeftShift) or UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.RightShift),
				meta = false,
			}
			-- Mac meta probe: pcall because LeftMeta enum may not exist on all Studio runtimes.
			pcall(function()
				combo.meta = UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.LeftMeta) or UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.RightMeta)
			end)
			if not Bindings.isValidCombo(combo) then return end  -- modifier-only-key skip
			if _commitCombo(capturingActionId, combo) then _stopCapture("commit") end
		end)
		-- Also register through ConnectionManager so plugin teardown disconnects
		-- the capture listener if the user disables the plugin mid-bind.
		if Connections then Connections["ShortcutsCapture"] = _captureConn end
	end

	-- =========================================================
	-- Leader capture flow
	-- Mirrors chord capture but with KeyCode-only validation (no modifiers).
	-- _leaderCapturing + _leaderCaptureConn are forward-declared near the top so
	-- _startCapture can mutually-exclude with this flow.
	-- =========================================================

	local function _refreshLeaderLabel()
		if not leaderLabel then return end
		local lk = Bindings.getLeaderKey(_settings)
		if lk == false then
			leaderLabel.Text = "Leader: (none)"
			leaderLabel.TextColor3 = T.MutedGold
		else
			leaderLabel.Text = "Leader: " .. tostring(lk)
			leaderLabel.TextColor3 = T.BrightGold
		end
	end

	local function _stopLeaderCapture(_reason)
		if _leaderCaptureConn then _leaderCaptureConn:Disconnect(); _leaderCaptureConn = nil end
		_leaderCapturing = false
		_refreshLeaderLabel()
	end

	-- Reject modifier-only keys at capture time so the picker can't bind LeftShift /
	-- Ctrl / Alt / Meta as a leader (would never produce a "non-leader" keypress).
	local LEADER_MODIFIER_REJECT = {
		LeftControl = true, RightControl = true, LeftAlt = true, RightAlt = true,
		LeftShift = true, RightShift = true, LeftMeta = true, RightMeta = true,
		LeftSuper = true, RightSuper = true,
	}

	local function _startLeaderCapture()
		if _leaderCaptureConn then _stopLeaderCapture("rearm") end
		-- Mutual exclusion with chord capture; otherwise the next keypress would
		-- commit as both a chord binding AND a leader.
		if _captureConn then _stopCapture("leader-rearm") end
		mod.ensureSettings()
		_leaderCapturing = true
		if leaderLabel then
			leaderLabel.Text = "Press leader key... (Esc cancels)"
			leaderLabel.TextColor3 = T.BrightGold
		end
		_leaderCaptureConn = UserInputService.InputBegan:Connect(function(input)
			if input.UserInputType ~= Enum.UserInputType.Keyboard then return end
			if input.KeyCode == Enum.KeyCode.Escape then _stopLeaderCapture("escape"); return end
			if UserInputService:GetFocusedTextBox() then return end
			local kcName = input.KeyCode.Name
			if LEADER_MODIFIER_REJECT[kcName] then return end
			local clean, ok = Bindings.isValidLeader(kcName)
			if not ok then return end
			_settings.leaderKey = clean
			Bindings.save(plugin, _settings)
			_fireChanged()
			_stopLeaderCapture("commit")
			mod.populate()  -- chord display labels refresh with new leader prefix
		end)
		if Connections then Connections["ShortcutsLeaderCapture"] = _leaderCaptureConn end
	end

	local function _clearLeader()
		mod.ensureSettings()
		if _leaderCaptureConn then _stopLeaderCapture("clear") end
		_settings.leaderKey = false
		Bindings.save(plugin, _settings)
		_fireChanged()
		_refreshLeaderLabel()
		mod.populate()
	end

	-- =========================================================
	-- Row builder
	-- =========================================================

	local function _makeRow(parent, actionId, def, layoutOrder)
		-- Matches UIBuilder convention: Settings panel + Properties rows wrap text in
		-- W.makeBlob (themed background + corner + stroke) and use W.makeLabel for
		-- typography. Plain TextLabels on a transparent row would read as floating
		-- text  -  inconsistent with the rest of the plugin. Row height 24 matches
		-- Settings AERow/USRow.
		local row = Instance.new("Frame")
		row.Name = "Row_" .. actionId
		row.BackgroundTransparency = 1
		row.Size = UDim2.new(1, -4, 0, 24)
		row.LayoutOrder = layoutOrder
		row.Parent = parent

		-- nameBlob fixed at 130px (action names short + bounded). comboBlob fills the
		-- middle minus the right-side button gutter (78px = 22 X + 40 Bind + 16 gaps).
		-- Name blob (left): themed pill with action display name. Internal padding via
		-- UIPadding so text doesn't sit flush against the rounded corner.
		local nameBlob = W.makeBlob("Name", row, UDim2.new(0, 130, 1, -2))
		nameBlob.Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 1)
		W.addPadding(nameBlob, 6, 4, 0, 0)
		local nameLabel = W.makeLabel("L", nameBlob, def.displayName or actionId, T.MutedGold, T.Font, 10)
		nameLabel.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left
		nameLabel.TextTruncate = Enum.TextTruncate.AtEnd

		-- Combo blob (middle): themed pill showing current binding / suggestion / "(unbound)".
		-- Same treatment as the name blob for visual consistency.
		-- comboBlob right reserve = 208 (74px button gutter) so the bind button sits
		-- close to comboBlob's right edge.
		local comboBlob = W.makeBlob("Combo", row, UDim2.new(1, -208, 1, -2))
		comboBlob.Position = UDim2.new(0, 134, 0, 1)
		W.addPadding(comboBlob, 6, 4, 0, 0)
		local comboLabel = W.makeLabel("L", comboBlob, "(unbound)", T.BrightGold, T.Font, 10)
		comboLabel.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left
		comboLabel.TextTruncate = Enum.TextTruncate.AtEnd

		-- Right-anchored buttons. Layout: [...nameBlob...][...comboBlob...] [Bind][X].
		-- Offsets from right edge: X (22) flush at -4; Bind (40) at -(4+22+4)=-30.
		local unbindBtn = W.makeButton("Unbind_"..actionId, row, "X", UDim2.new(0, 22, 1, -4), T.DarkGold)
		unbindBtn.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(1, 0)
		unbindBtn.Position = UDim2.new(1, -4, 0, 2)
		unbindBtn.TextSize = 10

		local bindBtn = W.makeButton("Bind_"..actionId, row, "Bind", UDim2.new(0, 40, 1, -4), T.DarkGold)
		bindBtn.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(1, 0)
		bindBtn.Position = UDim2.new(1, -30, 0, 2)
		bindBtn.TextSize = 10

		bindBtn.Activated:Connect(function() _startCapture(actionId) end)
		unbindBtn.Activated:Connect(function()
			-- Stop ANY armed capture, not just one matching this row. Clicking X on
			-- a different row while another is in "Press key..." mode would otherwise
			-- leave the original listener alive after populate() destroyed its prompt.
			if _captureConn then _stopCapture("unbind") end
			_settings.bindings[actionId] = nil
			Bindings.save(plugin, _settings)
			_fireChanged()
			mod.populate()
		end)

		_rows[actionId] = {
			frame = row, comboLabel = comboLabel,
			bindBtn = bindBtn, unbindBtn = unbindBtn,
		}
		return row
	end

	local function _makeCategoryHeader(parent, name, layoutOrder)
		-- Matches BuildProperties section-header style  -  slightly taller, gold accent,
		-- with a small left padding so the label doesn't sit flush.
		local hdr = Instance.new("Frame")
		hdr.Name = "Cat_" .. name
		hdr.BackgroundTransparency = 1
		hdr.Size = UDim2.new(1, -4, 0, 20)
		hdr.LayoutOrder = layoutOrder
		hdr.Parent = parent
		W.addPadding(hdr, 4, 0, 4, 0)
		local lbl = W.makeLabel("L", hdr, name, T.Gold, T.Font, 11)
		lbl.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left
	end

	-- =========================================================
	-- populate / filter
	-- =========================================================

	function mod.populate()
		-- Clear existing rows + headers (preserve placeholder if no actions; safe to drop it
		-- since populate runs after _settings is loaded).
		for _, child in ipairs(scrollList:GetChildren()) do
			if child:IsA("Frame") or (child:IsA("TextLabel") and child.Name:sub(1,4) == "Cat_") or child.Name == "Placeholder" then
				child:Destroy()
			end
		end
		_rows = {}
		local filter = (searchBox and searchBox.Text or ""):lower()
		-- Group by category, ordered: UI, Edit, Animate, Emit, Editor.
		local categoryOrder = {"UI", "Tools", "Edit", "Animate", "Emit", "Editor"}
		local byCat = {}
		for actionId, def in pairs(Actions) do
			-- Filter to implemented actions only  -  stubs (ResetSelection,
			-- OpenGraphEditor, OpenColorPicker) shouldn't appear in the bindable list.
			if def.implemented == true then
				local matchesFilter = filter == "" or
					(def.displayName or actionId):lower():find(filter, 1, true) ~= nil or
					actionId:lower():find(filter, 1, true) ~= nil
				if matchesFilter then
					local cat = def.category or "Other"
					byCat[cat] = byCat[cat] or {}
					table.insert(byCat[cat], {actionId = actionId, def = def})
				end
			end
		end
		local layoutOrder = 0
		for _, cat in ipairs(categoryOrder) do
			local rows = byCat[cat]
			if rows and #rows > 0 then
				_makeCategoryHeader(scrollList, cat, layoutOrder); layoutOrder = layoutOrder + 1
				-- Stable per-category order: alphabetical actionId.
				table.sort(rows, function(a, b) return a.actionId < b.actionId end)
				for _, entry in ipairs(rows) do
					_makeRow(scrollList, entry.actionId, entry.def, layoutOrder)
					-- Refresh combo label. Unbound rows read "(unbound)"; bound rows show
					-- the actual combo. An active conflict notice for this row overlays a
					-- red message instead.
					local combo = _settings.bindings[entry.actionId]
					local cl = _rows[entry.actionId].comboLabel
					if _conflictNotice and _conflictNotice.actionId == entry.actionId and os.clock() < _conflictNotice.expiresAt then
						cl.Text = _conflictNotice.message
						cl.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(220, 80, 80)
					else
						cl.Text = combo and Bindings.formatCombo(combo, _isMac, Bindings.getLeaderKey(_settings)) or "(unbound)"
						cl.TextColor3 = T.MutedGold
					end
					layoutOrder = layoutOrder + 1
				end
			end
		end
	end

	-- =========================================================
	-- ensureSettings / Reset / open / close
	-- =========================================================

	-- Runtime attaches at plugin setup BEFORE the user has opened the panel.
	-- getSettings() must return a populated table, so prime _settings lazily on
	-- first access instead of at open() time.
	function mod.ensureSettings()
		if _settings == nil then
			-- Defense-in-depth: Bindings.load already normalizes the version field,
			-- but any other unforeseen error inside load() must NOT abort plugin
			-- bootstrap. Fall back to defaults on any error.
			local ok, result = pcall(Bindings.load, plugin, Actions)
			if ok and type(result) == "table" then
				_settings = result
			else
				warn("[Part-Icles Shortcuts] Bindings.load failed; using defaults: "..tostring(result))
				_settings = {version = Bindings.VERSION, overlayEnabled = true, bindings = Bindings._copyDefaults()}
			end
		end
		return _settings
	end

	-- Two-click reset confirm. First click flips the button to a confirm state; the
	-- second click within `_resetConfirmWindow` seconds commits. Auto-reverts after
	-- the window with task.delay.
	local _resetArmed = false
	local _resetArmedAt = 0
	local _resetConfirmWindow = 3
	local _resetOriginalText = resetBtn and resetBtn.Text or "Unbind all"
	local function _disarmReset()
		_resetArmed = false
		if resetBtn then resetBtn.Text = _resetOriginalText end
	end
	function mod.reset()
		mod.ensureSettings()
		_settings.bindings = Bindings._copyDefaults()
		Bindings.save(plugin, _settings)
		_disarmReset()
		-- Tear down any armed capture so a post-reset keypress doesn't silently
		-- rebind a row the user just told us to clear.
		if _captureConn then _stopCapture("reset") end
		_fireChanged()
		mod.populate()
	end
	local function _onResetClick()
		if not _open then return end
		if _resetArmed and (os.clock() - _resetArmedAt) <= _resetConfirmWindow then
			mod.reset()
			return
		end
		_resetArmed = true
		_resetArmedAt = os.clock()
		if resetBtn then resetBtn.Text = "Click again to confirm" end
		task.delay(_resetConfirmWindow, function()
			-- Bail if the user already clicked through. Otherwise restore label.
			if _resetArmed and (os.clock() - _resetArmedAt) >= _resetConfirmWindow - 0.05 then
				_disarmReset()
			end
		end)
	end

	function mod.open()
		if _open then return end
		_open = true
		mod.ensureSettings()
		_refreshIsMac()  -- re-read plugin setting so label preference picks up flips.
		_refreshLeaderLabel()
		panel.Visible = true
		mod.populate()
	end

	function mod.close()
		if not _open then return end
		_open = false
		_stopCapture("close")
		_stopLeaderCapture("close")
		_disarmReset()
		panel.Visible = false
	end

	-- Plugin-teardown hook; cancels pending conflict-notice timer + an in-flight
	-- capture's InputBegan listener (otherwise the disconnect-on-stop path never runs
	-- when the user toggles plugin off mid-capture, leaving an orphan Connection).
	function mod.destroy()
		_destroyed = true
		if _captureConn then _captureConn:Disconnect(); _captureConn = nil end
		_captureActionId = nil
		if _leaderCaptureConn then _leaderCaptureConn:Disconnect(); _leaderCaptureConn = nil end
		_leaderCapturing = false
		if _conflictTimer then pcall(task.cancel, _conflictTimer); _conflictTimer = nil end
		_conflictNotice = nil
	end

	function mod.isOpen() return _open end
	function mod.isCapturing() return _captureActionId ~= nil or _leaderCapturing end

	function mod.getSettings()
		-- Runtime safety: if dispatcher loads before user opens the panel, prime defaults so
		-- the 3 pre-bound shortcuts still fire on first install.
		return mod.ensureSettings()
	end

	-- Runtime registers a callback here; Wiring fires it after every save (commit /
	-- unbind / reset) so the reverse-index rebuilds. Single-consumer hook  -  replace
	-- with a Signal if a second consumer ever needs it.
	function mod.setOnChanged(callback)
		_onChanged = callback
	end

	-- Register signal connections through ConnectionManager so plugin teardown
	-- disconnects them (consistent with every other top-level wiring path).
	if Connections then
		if searchBox then
			Connections["ShortcutsSearchChanged"] = searchBox:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Text"):Connect(function()
				if _open then mod.populate() end
			end)
		end
		if resetBtn then
			Connections["ShortcutsReset"] = resetBtn.Activated:Connect(_onResetClick)
		end
		if leaderSetBtn then
			Connections["ShortcutsLeaderSet"] = leaderSetBtn.Activated:Connect(_startLeaderCapture)
		end
		if leaderClearBtn then
			Connections["ShortcutsLeaderClear"] = leaderClearBtn.Activated:Connect(_clearLeader)
		end
	else
		-- Defensive fallback if Bootstrap forgets to pass Connections. Module is plugin-lifetime
		-- so leak risk is small but warn so the gap surfaces in dev.
		warn("[Part-Icles Shortcuts] Wiring built without Connections  -  search/reset signals are dangling")
		if searchBox then searchBox:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Text"):Connect(function() if _open then mod.populate() end end) end
		if resetBtn then resetBtn.Activated:Connect(_onResetClick) end
		if leaderSetBtn then leaderSetBtn.Activated:Connect(_startLeaderCapture) end
		if leaderClearBtn then leaderClearBtn.Activated:Connect(_clearLeader) end
	end

	return mod
end

--[[
	UIBuilder Module - Part-Icles V5
	Copyright (C) 2026 Qwinkle
	Orchestrates all UI construction. Delegates to UIBuilderConstants, UIWidgets, UIToolPanels.
]]

-- task.wait between requires spreads obfuscated VM bootstrap across frames so the
-- initial UIBuilder load doesn't pile onto the same frame as Part's mixin chain.
local C = require(script.Constants); task.wait()
local W = require(script.Widgets); task.wait()
local TP = require(script.ToolPanels); task.wait()
local BP = require(script.BuildProperties); task.wait()
local IP = require(script.InventoryPanel); task.wait()

local T = C.T
local LAYOUT = C.LAYOUT

local UIBuilder = {}
-- Module-scoped (not self-state): persists across SnapshotTheme/RestoreTheme cycles so the descendant-walk
-- inside UpdateTheme can short-circuit when the same font is re-applied. Walking ~1000+ descendants per
-- color-picker drag was a measurable cost; this skip relies on font being a string-name comparison.
local _currentFontName = T.Font.Name

-- BUILD HUD
local function buildHUD(screenGui)
